fact: Semlex said its biometric ID agreement was signed on 16 May 2018 as a build-operate-transfer arrangement and that transfer of the system to the Gambian government was completed on 22 March 2024.

Subsequent reporting found immigration officials complained of being denied access to systems including the Orbis administrative database and firewall infrastructure, which reportedly remained under Semlex's control.
A Gambia Immigration Department officer testified on 6 October 2026 that the department no longer has access to the Semlex data because its access ended when the Semlex contract ended.
The new biometric card is rolled out by the Gambia Immigration Department, whose officers run the enrolment centres, under the system launched through the Ministry of Interior with Margins ID Group.

Margins ID Systems Ltd will design, build, co-operate and fund the new ID system for eight years under a build, co-operate and transfer model, sharing revenue 70/30 with the Government, with all assets transferred to the Government at the end.
Margins ID Systems Applications, a Ghanaian firm's subsidiary, won a build, co-operate and transfer contract with the Ministry of Interior for the national ID infrastructure.
source_slug: 2026-01-22 The Gambia picks Margins ID Group for national ID infrastructure upgrade

fact: MIDSA, a subsidiary of Ghana's Margins ID Group, was awarded the contract in January 2026 to design, deploy and operate the National Identity Management System under a Build, Operate and Transfer agreement.

President Barrow said the unified digital ID system will be locally designed, built, operated and managed by government services to ensure knowledge transfer and ownership, and that the concession contract for the National ID system will soon be replaced.
